display.text: With sample size and other design features fixed, lowering α generally reduces Type I error risk but increases Type II error risk; the consequences of both errors inform the chosen significance level.
The probability of correctly rejecting H₀ when a specified alternative is true; power = 1 − β. Larger samples generally increase power with other factors fixed.
Rejecting H₀ when it is true: a false positive conclusion that evidence supports an effect or departure that is absent.
Failing to reject H₀ when it is false: missing a real effect or departure from the null claim.
The probability of failing to reject H₀ for a specified true alternative. It depends on the effect, sample size, and testing procedure. Notation: β.
